title: Exploring Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Business Automation in Business Central
summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers enable AI agents to interact with Business Central data and perform actions like querying, creating, and modifying records. The post explains MCP concepts, demonstrates setting up an MCP server for the sales quote process, configuring it in Copilot Studio, and highlights security considerations such as limiting data exposure through custom APIs.
key_points: The post presents MCP as the next step after the Common Data Model, standardizing actions, data and reasoning surfaces for AI agents
An MCP server configuration in Business Central should have a clear goal and scope, with read, create, modify, delete and bound action permissions set per API
Copilot Studio offers a ready-made Business Central MCP tool that connects to an environment, a server configuration and a company, so an agent can create sales quotes through conversation
The Agent Tasks view in Copilot Studio shows the agent finding the operations and schemas the MCP server exposes
Anything exposed through MCP becomes reachable from outside, so purpose-built custom APIs should be used to limit which fields are shared

quotes.text: MCP standardizes actions, data, and reasoning surfaces for agents.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains how MCP extends beyond CDM to enable AI agents to interact with business systems in a standardized way

quotes.text: If you expose it to the MCP server it is available to the world!
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights the critical security implication that exposed APIs become accessible externally, requiring careful configuration

quotes.text: By creating a purpose build API we can choose the field and functions available and limit the risk of unintended data exposure.
quotes.why_it_matters: Provides the security solution of using custom APIs instead of standard APIs to control what data agents can access
